questions.stem:
The discrete random variable $R$ has the distribution $R \sim \mathrm{B}(n,p)$

The mean of $R$ is 200

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) State the variance of $R$ in terms of $p$
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) $200(1-p)$ oe as variance. Must be seen in (a). isw if they subsequently square root to find sd or multiply out and make errors B1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A normal distribution is used as an approximation for $R$

Using this approximation, $\mathrm{P}(R<180)=0.0307$ to 3 significant figures.

(b) Show that $\sqrt{200-200p}=10.96$ to 4 significant figures.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) $(z=)\pm\frac{179.5-200}{"\sqrt{200(1-p)}"}$ M1: attempt at continuity correction, sight of 179.5 or 180.5 may be implied by 19.5 or 20.5 imp. by a correct equation. M1: standardisation using their Normal distribution $\mathrm{N}(200,(a))$ (Note use of 220.5 for 179.5 and $z=1.87$ implied by a correct equation. Condone use of 180 for this mark. Allow use of $200(1-p)$ in (b) if (a) is incorrect. A1ft: for correct standardisation, ft their variance. Must have scored M1M1. $z=(\pm)1.87$ B1: awrt $\pm 1.87$ calculator gives $-1.8706$ $\frac{179.5-200}{\sqrt{200(1-p)}}=-1.87$ $*\sqrt{200(1-p)}=\frac{-20.5}{-1.87}=10.962\ldots*$ A1*cso: cso for achieving awrt 10.963 following a correct equation i.e. when their standardised expression is equated to $\pm 1.87$ the signs must be compatible otherwise A0*. If using a calculator to find the z-value look for awrt 10.959. $\frac{179.5-200}{\sqrt{200(1-p)}}=-1.87$ oe scores M1M1A1ftB1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Hence find the value of $p$, giving your answer to 2 significant figures.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (c) $1-p=0.600889\ldots$ or $200-200p=\frac{75076}{625}(=120.1216) \Rightarrow 200p=\frac{49924}{625}(=79.8784)$ M1: for rearranging the given answer to part (b) to $1-p=$ awrt 0.6 oe or $200p=$ awrt 80 oe using the correct order of operations. Implied by awrt 0.4. May also rearrange to $p=\frac{10.96^2-200}{-200}$ or equivalent which implies this mark. $p=0.39911\ldots$ awrt $p=0.40$ A1: awrt 0.40, use of 10.96 gives 0.399392

parts.label: a
parts.technique: in spec
parts.reason: question dropped: other parts out of spec

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Poisson approximation to binomial
parts.reason: Requires use of the Poisson distribution as an approximation. Poisson distribution is not named anywhere in the specification statements, so this is out.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Percentage error using Poisson approximation result
parts.reason: This part only makes sense using the answer from the out-of-spec Poisson approximation in (b), so it is out per the rule that dependent parts are out.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Conditions for Poisson approximation to binomial
parts.reason: Asks for conditions under which Poisson approximates binomial - Poisson is not covered in the spec at all.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Solving simultaneous equations from Poisson probability formulae
parts.reason: Requires forming equations using the Poisson pmf, which is not part of the specification.

parts.label: (i)(a)(b)
parts.technique: Statistic vs parameter concept
parts.reason: This concerns 'statistic' and 'sampling distribution' terminology which is not mentioned anywhere in the specification statements (only simple random sampling etc. under S1.1, not the concept of a statistic as an estimator or sampling distribution).

parts.label: ii
parts.technique: Sampling distribution of a discrete random variable / order comparison
parts.reason: Explicitly framed as 'sampling distribution' of Y, a named concept not mentioned in the specification statements (only probability topics S3.1-S3.3 mention independent events but not sampling distributions of random variables).

parts.label: iii(a)
parts.technique: Listing outcomes from sampling without replacement
parts.reason: This is part of building a sampling distribution (explicitly named later in the question, part (c)), a concept not covered in the spec statements.

parts.label: iii(b)
parts.technique: Listing values of derived random variable T
parts.reason: Continues building toward the sampling distribution of T, not covered by any spec statement.

parts.label: iii(c)
parts.technique: Sampling distribution of T
parts.reason: Explicitly asks for the 'sampling distribution' of T, a named concept absent from the specification statements.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Probability density function of continuous uniform distribution
parts.reason: Requires finding a pdf. S4.2 explicitly states 'Knowledge of the probability density function is not required'.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Sketch pdf graph
parts.reason: Sketching a probability density function - excluded per S4.2 exclusion of pdf knowledge.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Mean of continuous uniform distribution
parts.reason: Finding mean of a continuous random variable defined via pdf; pdf knowledge and this distribution are not in the spec.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Cumulative distribution function
parts.reason: S4.2 excludes derivation of cumulative distribution function knowledge, and cdf/pdf work generally is not covered anywhere in the statements.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: E(Y) for Y=X^2 using pdf integration
parts.reason: Requires integrating using the pdf, explicitly excluded (S4.2) and not part of any statement.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Probability calculation using pdf/cdf
parts.reason: Based on the pdf/cdf of the continuous uniform distribution, excluded topic.

parts.label: i(a)
parts.technique: E(X^2) via integration of a given pdf
parts.reason: Explicitly uses a probability density function f(x), which S4.2 states knowledge of is not required.

parts.label: i(b)
parts.technique: Var(X) from E(X) and E(X^2) of continuous r.v. with pdf
parts.reason: Depends on the out-of-spec pdf-based E(X^2) from part (a), and Var(X) of a continuous rv via pdf is not in the specification.

parts.label: ii(a)
parts.technique: Binomial probability regarding order statistics relative to quartile
parts.reason: Although the arithmetic resembles binomial probability, the setup relies on continuous random variable Y and its quartiles (probability density function context), a topic combination not covered by the specification.

parts.label: ii(b)
parts.technique: Binomial probability regarding order statistics relative to quartile
parts.reason: Same as (ii)(a): depends on continuous distribution quartile context not in spec.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Poisson probability calculations
parts.reason: Requires modelling meteors with Poisson distribution; Poisson is not covered anywhere in the specification statements.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Hypotheses for Poisson mean test
parts.reason: Hypothesis test framed in terms of Poisson parameter λ; the specification's hypothesis testing statements (S5.2, S5.3) only cover binomial proportion and Normal mean, not Poisson.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Critical region for Poisson hypothesis test
parts.reason: Based on Poisson distribution, not covered by the specification's hypothesis testing statements.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Conclusion of Poisson hypothesis test
parts.reason: Depends on the out-of-spec Poisson-based critical region from (c).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Sketch pdf
parts.reason: Sketching a given probability density function; S4.2 excludes knowledge of pdf.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Mode of continuous distribution from pdf
parts.reason: Mode identified from a pdf graph, part of the excluded pdf topic.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.technique: Finding normalising constant k by integrating pdf
parts.reason: Requires integrating a given probability density function to find k such that total probability is 1; explicit pdf exclusion under S4.2 applies.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.technique: Verifying upper quartile using pdf integration
parts.reason: Uses integration of the pdf to locate a quartile, excluded topic (pdf knowledge not required, S4.2), and depends on the out-of-spec k from (c)(i).
